title: Tell the Account instead of asking it

task.text: `Teller` reads an account's balance and overdraft, decides, then writes the new balance back.

Move the rule to where the data lives, so no caller can forget it. `Teller.withdraw` and `Teller.transfer` must return and change exactly what they do now, including leaving everything untouched when they refuse.

items: `boolean Account.withdraw(long amount)`: false and no change when `amount` exceeds balance plus overdraft.
`Teller` keeps its two methods but never reads or writes account state.

checks.title: Account no longer exposes setBalance or the overdraft

hints.text: Count how many times `Teller` reaches into `Account` for numbers it then computes with. The rule "can this be afforded?" is knowledge about the account, so it belongs inside it.

Give `Account` `withdraw(long)` that checks and mutates itself, and `deposit(long)`. `Teller.withdraw` becomes one delegating call, and `transfer` tells one account to withdraw and the other to deposit.
